sections.content:
29,395 people

were counted on the census as "taxation experts" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Taxation experts advise on tax matters and assess tax liabilities.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "taxation experts" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "taxation experts", 15.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "taxation experts" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "taxation experts" included:

  • engineering professionals (other)
  • interior designers
  • medical and dental technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "taxation experts" there were a similar number of men and women (52.6% compared with 47.4%).

This means "taxation experts" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 52.6% and women made up 47.4% of "taxation experts"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "taxation experts" included:

  • horticultural trades
  • higher education teaching professionals
  • debt, rent and other cash collectors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "taxation experts" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "taxation experts" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "taxation experts", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84% compared with 16%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.4%) than self-employed (9.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
